title: My robot vacuum runs at 3 AM. Its map shows someone standing in my hallway.
story:
Bump. Pause. Bump. At three in the morning, my robot vacuum was ramming into the same empty spot in my hallway, again and again.

I set it to clean at night because I sleep through anything. Every morning, the app shows a map of my apartment, with a little gray outline on the bed where it bumped around me.

Last week, a second gray shape showed up on the map. In the hallway. Standing still, about as wide as a person.

Each night, the shape was a little closer to my bedroom. So tonight, I didn't go to bed. I sat on the floor at the end of the hall, phone in hand, and waited.

At three, the vacuum rolled out. It bumped the empty air in front of me. Once. Twice. On the map, the shape appeared, close enough to touch.

Then it went quiet. The vacuum turned around and rolled into my bedroom, and I watched the map draw itself. The dresser. The closet. The bed.

The little gray outline was on the bed, right where I always sleep. But I was out here, in the hall, staring at my phone.

Then the outline sat up.
premise: robot vacuum's nightly map shows a person-shaped obstacle creeping down the hall; the narrator stays up, and the map still shows someone lying in his bed
